result.title: North Kingstown Town Council Meeting Summary - March 24, 2025
result.creator: OpenPublica
result.description: # North Kingstown Town Council Meeting - March 24, 2025 The North Kingstown Town Council met on Monday, March 24, 2025, at 7:00 PM in Town Hall Council Chambers, 80 Boston Neck Road. The Council held public hearings, received a Safe Streets for All presentation, heard public comment, approved a routine consent calendar, accepted manager and finance reports, acted on coastal applications, and made appointments. The meeting opened with a flag salute and a moment of silence for George Hammond, Peggy Fitzpatrick, and Nicholas Moussom Mesamucci. ### Public Hearings - Item 4 - Second reading of an ordinance amending Chapter 13 (Public Beaches), including enforcement, use by nonresidents, and beach parking permits. The hearing was opened and closed, and the ordinance was approved by voice vote. - Item 5 - Second reading of an ordinance amending Section 9-4, Table VI (Recreation Department fees for beach parking permits). The hearing was closed without on-microphone testimony, and the ordinance was approved by voice vote. ### Safe Streets for All Safety Action Plan Presentation - Bowman Engineering, with Planning staff, presented the draft Safety Action Plan developed through the RIPTA-led Safe Streets and Roads for All grant program. It is a $6.25 million joint project involving $5 million in federal funds, $1.25 million in state capital funds, and 31 of Rhode Island's 39 municipalities, with no local match. - Crash data from 2019 through 2023 show North Kingstown ranked 21st out of 39 municipalities in crash rate; pedestrians and bicyclists face higher injury risk than motor vehicle occupants, and crashes trend toward afternoons, Fridays, and Saturdays. - Fourteen locations were selected and ranked, with recommended countermeasures including higher-visibility crosswalks, ADA-compliant curb ramps, signal visibility improvements, and related safety upgrades. - Public input included tabling at Harbor Fire and Casey Farm farmers market, stakeholder interviews, and a statewide survey with North Kingstown zip codes separated out. - The plan is in final editing; an implementation grant notice of funding opportunity is expected within about three weeks or by mid-April, though federal requirements affecting climate and equity language are uncertain. - Council members asked about implementation grant certainty, education and enforcement components, coordination with RIDOT, possible bike lanes, and census data on households without cars. - The Council authorized the Council President to sign a letter of support for the Safety Action Plan. ### Public Comments & Testimony - John Mashada asked for Ryan Park trail maintenance funding, noting he led volunteers for over 100 hours in 2024, identified 20 muddy spots, and requested DPW and Recreation annual trail maintenance. - Dan Moning urged the Council to disclose electric aggregation contract rates and terms. He noted the statewide regulated rate is currently about 16 cents and is scheduled to drop to 10.1 cents on April 1, and that savings estimates must account for delivery versus supply portions of the bill. - Karen Salvatore asked that traffic signal timing be included in the safety plan and that new signal fixtures be attractive and consistent with North Kingstown's local character. - Richard Welch raised concerns about the school project's cost and two-story design, cited RIDE criticism, and asked the Council to stop the process and re-engage former facilities committee members. - Brett Mallory supported redistricting and criticized school bond management and Council leadership, urging stronger direction to the School Committee. - Tom Saguras asked the town to push RIPTA for reliable bus connections, describing the Route 14 detour to Wickford Junction as unreliable; he also invited residents to a Rhode Island Transit Riders event on April 7. - Meg Kerr thanked staff for the comprehensive plan implementation report but noted the annual review requirement had been missed; she asked the Council to restore annual Planning Commission and Council reviews and pointed to gaps in home energy audit and solar outreach. - Bob Vanderslice supported the report and suggested clearer next steps, School Department participation, and stronger town advocacy for decarbonization; he noted a 37-person waitlist for a library sustainable landscaping talk. - Many Lone Tree Point and Earle Drive area residents, including Sue Alexander, David Fawcett, Joyce Pastore, Bobby Robertson, Kristen Flynn, Jen Meegan, Amy and Joseph Denhoff, Jennifer Tha, Mary Warbeck, Linda Teraborelli, Lincoln Monroe, and Heather Hole, opposed the proposed dock at 353 Earle Drive. Concerns included swimming and kayak safety, limited depth at low tide, location inside the mooring field, the requested 72.5-foot extension beyond mean low water, shellfish and salt marsh impacts, potential rental use by inexperienced boaters, and harm to the beach's character. - Mary Walbeck asked which design standards the town uses, citing ASCE recommendations for sea level rise, increased precipitation, and the 500-year floodplain as important for permitting and infrastructure decisions. ### Consent Calendar - Items 8 through 20 were approved in one motion with no items removed. These included minutes of February 24, 2025; Tax Abatement List #880 in the amount of $504.65; a $1,100 donation for Al's Kids Recreation Program scholarships; a Code Enforcement Ford Explorer purchase from Tasca Ford for $37,878.50; award of 15 fire hydrants to John Hoadley and Sons for $49,875; an OPEB actuarial services contract with Conrad Siegel, Inc. for $7,000 in FY2025, $750 in FY2026, and $7,000 in FY2027; a Wilson Park mobile food concession award to Matt Picard, dba The Snack Bar, for $501; renewal of the town's annual entertainment license; authorization to apply for the T-Mobile Hometown Grant for the Wickford Village Wayfinding Initiative; acceptance of the Learn365 and Math Matters RI Grant for $55,000; acceptance of a $480 Life Safety and Emergency Action Grant for beach Go-Bags; acceptance of a $1,250 Safety and Risk Management Scholarship for conflict resolution training; and a joint utility pole placement by Rhode Island Energy and Verizon on Roger Williams Drive. ### Town Manager's Report - The school building subcommittee voted on March 12 to move forward with seeking new architecture and engineering and owner's project management firms; the committee also discussed project labor agreements and an updated demographic study for RIDE. The Council noted that final contracts require Council approval. - The public safety complex project now meets weekly; discussion included the QDC site purchase, environmental and geotechnical studies, cash flow needs, and reducing the footprint to fit the bond. - Revolution Wind work in Quonset Business Park includes over 200 workers per day on daytime shifts; an emergency drill was held March 12. - The Wickford Waterfront Streetscape work stoppage is being handled by the town solicitor, with an update expected April 14. - RIDOT revised bridge project plans after public safety concerns: the South County Trail Bridge will have no closures, and the Frenchtown Road Bridge will have limited night closures without blocking emergency apparatus; coordination meetings will continue every other week. - The Post Road and West Main Street sidewalk project is expected to be advertised this summer with construction in 2026; the mini roundabout project is expected to be advertised next month with construction this fall and outreach to Wickford businesses and residents. - The manager reported a lunch with Governor McKee and other municipal leaders, discussed federal earmark cancellations and reapplications, and presented town priorities including education funding, road programs, housing policy, and unfunded mandates. - The Rhode Island Interlocal Trust notified the town of a 10.16% health premium increase, a 6.29% dental increase, and a 49.39% workers' compensation increase. The manager said these amounts exceeded budget assumptions and that staff are reworking the budget to avoid a tax-rate impact, with options to be presented before the April 21 public hearing. ### Good Energy Update - The town signed an electric service agreement with NextEra Energy Services, contingent on rates below last-resort service at launch. - The planned June launch was delayed because market prices have risen; Good Energy recommended renegotiating in October and November and moving outreach to late summer or fall. ### Finance Director's Report - The Finance Director projected revenues $1,716,122 over budget, driven by earnings on invested funds, police detail revenue, and tangible personal property tax revenue, while reducing expected revenue from the delayed Wickford L sale. - The projected year-end surplus is currently $1,185,122, subject to changes from open positions, overtime, and department spending. - Council discussion focused on whether to use projected surplus to offset FY2026 insurance increases. The manager cautioned against creating a structural deficit and stated the FY2027 goal remains no tax increase despite debt pressures in FY2028. ### Comprehensive Plan Implementation Report - Planning staff presented the five-year resilience-oriented implementation report for the 2019 Comprehensive Plan. A full implementation report is expected in coming months, and annual reporting that had been missed will resume. - School highlights included HVAC and energy-efficiency upgrades at multiple schools, new windows at Davisville Middle School, design of a new net-zero middle school using geothermal and rooftop solar, and food recycling programs that reduced trash sent to landfill by an average of 80% per elementary school. - The town may improve its Community Rating System flood insurance rating from Class 9, a 5% discount, to Class 7, a 15% discount. - Council members praised the report and agreed resiliency should be integrated into ongoing decision-making. ### CRMC Applications - Item 24 - Edon Realty Trust, c/o Donna Rossetti, requested a CRMC residential boating facility consisting of a fixed pier, ramp, and float at 353 Earle Drive. After extensive public comment, both the Harbor Management Commission and Conservation Commission unanimously recommended substantive objection. The Council voted to submit a substantive objection to CRMC. - Item 25 - Quonset Development Corporation requested CRMC approval for a wave attenuator system along the north side of the Pier 2 extension at the Port of Davisville. The Council voted to file no substantive objection. ### Appointments and Correspondence - The Council appointed one Arts Council applicant to a term ending March 1, 2026, and voted to reduce the Arts Council from 13 to 10 members. - The Council appointed Max Reynolds to the Zoning Board of Review as Second Alternate to July 1, 2026, filling the unexpired term of Richard Welch. - Correspondence included many emails about the Earle Drive dock, school redistricting and budget concerns, RIDE comments on the school project, and requests from Richard Welch regarding auto expense stipends, beach pass exemptions, and transfer station fees. ### Key Outcomes - Approved the Public Beaches ordinance amendment and the Recreation fee schedule ordinance amendment on second reading. - Authorized the Council President to sign the Safe Streets for All letter of support. - Approved the entire Consent Calendar, Items 8 through 20. - Voted to file a substantive objection to CRMC on the Earle Drive dock application. - Voted to file no substantive objection on the Quonset Development Corporation wave attenuator application. - Appointed an Arts Council member and reduced Arts Council membership to 10; appointed Max Reynolds to the Zoning Board. - Directed budget work to address insurance cost increases, with proposed solutions to be presented before the April 21 public hearing. The meeting adjourned after the Council completed its agenda.

result.title: Rhode Island History Digital Collection
result.description: The John Carter Brown Library and the Redwood Library and Athenaeum are Rhode Island institutions with distinct, but complementary, collections. To lay the foundation for a Rhode Island History Digital Collection the two libraries are collaborating on a project to scan the unique documents representing the earliest chapters of the region. The Redwood Library holds some unique manuscript records of early Rhode Island and the John Carter Brown Library holds seminal works by Roger Williams, Rhode Island's founder and innovator, as well as materials relating to religion, native peoples, conflicts with native peoples and the British government, boundary issues, business, daily life, and education. THE REDWOOD LIBRARY AND ATHENAEUM is one of the first lending libraries in America, housed in the oldest lending library building in the country. Founded in 1747 by forty-six proprietors upon the principle of "having nothing in view but the good of mankind," its mission continues over 265 years later. The Library's core collections include the original collection of 1522 volumes gathered by the first proprietors and printed materials related to the history of Newport and Aquidneck Island that far exceed the collecting scope of any other regional cultural institution. THE JOHN CARTER BROWN LIBRARY is an independently administered and funded center for advanced research in history and the humanities, founded in 1846 and located at Brown University since 1901. Housed within the library's walls is an internationally renowned collection of primary historical sources pertaining to North and South America from the time of its discovery by Europeans (ca. 1492) until the end of the colonial period (ca. 1825).

result.description: Die Pegasus 5.0 CDROM bietet Ihnen eine Sammlung von internationalen Shareware und Public-Domain Programmen. Als Zusatz gibt es eine Multimedia-Bonus-CDROM für Windows. (Alle Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten über 650 MB der aktuellsten und besten deutschen und internationalen Shareware-Programme. Die Auswahl der Programme erfolgte von einem Kenner der Shareware-Szene. Alle Dateibeschreibungen in Deutsch. Zwei Menüsysteme für DOS und Windows erlauben das automatische Entpacken und Kopieren der Dateien, Starten der Programme, Lesen von Textdateien und vieles mehr. FILES.BBS für den sofortigen Mailbox-Einsatz. Die unterschiedlichen Versionen der Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten so gut wie keine Duplikate von Programmen. Mit dieser Serie besitzen Sie somit eine der bestsortiertesten Shareware-Sammlungen der Welt.) TRADEWRK.ZIP 2813323 06-10-94 Tradework for Windows 1.0 ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonders übersichtlich und einfach zu bedienen. Tradework ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonderer Wert wurde auf Übersichtlichkeit und einfache Bedienung gelegt. Der Funktionsumfang von Tradework umfaß folgende Möglichkeiten: Angebote erfassen und daraus Aufträge generieren, Bestellwesen, Direkterfassung von Bestellungen und Aufträgen, Kunden- und Lieferantenverwaltung, Artikelverwaltung und Lagerführung, Mahnwesen, Umsatzstatistiken, offene Posten Kontrolle, Etikettendruck uvm. ANAGRA15.ZIP 77715 06-03-94 Anagrams v1.5, bildet aus einem Wort alle möglichen Buchstabenkombinationen Bildet anhand eines festen (englischen!) Wortschatzes ein Anagram (Buchstabenpuzzle) zu einem vorgebenen Wort oder Satz. Mit vielen Optionen zur Beeinflussung des Ergebnisses und relativ umfangreicher Dokumentationsdatei. ARZTPW.ZIP 1222995 12-06-94 Arztpraxis Wiegand, umfangreiches Verwaltungsprogramm für die Arztpraxis, relativ leistungsfähig (deutsch) Verwaltungsprogramm für Arztpraxen. Alle anfallenden Vorgänge von der Stammdatenerfassung für jeden Patienten über das Ausstellen von Mahnungen bis zum Quartalsabschluß können damit automatisiert werden. Zusätzlich lassen sich beliebige Datenbanken mit Patientendaten, Medikamenten usw. anlegen. Für Datensicherung sorgt eine automatische Back-Up-Funktion und eine Paßwort-Option. Verschiedene AddOn´s sind verfügbar, wie eine Dateienverwaltung für Hausbesuche und die Gelbe Liste Pharmindex (kostet DM 100 extra). Regelmäßige Updates zu Beginn eines jeden Quartals. BALG20.ZIP 116922 12-02-94 Basic Algebra v2.0, Algebra-Lernprogramm für Kinder und Erwachsene Einfaches Lern- und Übungsprogramm zum Training der Rechenfähigkeit. Auf erklärende Texte zu verschiedenen Themengebieten folgen Testaufgaben. Die Erfolgsquote wird sofort ermittelt und anschließend grafisch dargestellt. Der Lernstoff von Basic Algebra beschränkt sich auf die unterschiedlichen Zahlenarten, auf Brüche und Gleichungen. Das Programm führt übrigens bei jedem Programmstart einen automatischen Viren-Check durch. BEAM21.ZIP 49144 01-03-94 Beam v2.1, simple Statikberechnung von diversen Stahlträgerprofilen Programm zur Berechnung der statischen Eigenschaften von Trägerprofilen unterschiedlicher Ausmaße und Materialien. Alle relevanten Eigenschaften der Träger sind berücksichtigt und können vorgegeben werden. Das Tool ist Teil der umfangreichen Sammlung von Engineers Shareware (insgesamt über 60 Tools), die weitere Hilfsmittel für Berechnungen am Bau enthält (Registrierungsgebühr hierfür: US$ 195). Alle wichtigen Daten zur Beurteilung der Eignung eines Platzes sind vorhanden: Lage, Ausstattung, Serviceleistungen, mögliche Lärmbelästigungen, Nutzungsbedingungen (auf manchen Campingplätzen dürfen z.B. keine Caravans aufgestellt werden) und die ungefähre Preislage. Daneben erleichtert das Programm die Routenplanung und bietet die Möglichkeit, zu jedem Eintrag eigene Notizen zu machen. Eine Suchfunktion ist ebenfalls vorhanden. (Die Shareware-Version enthält nur Einträge aus dem Saarland und Schleswig-Holstein.) result.title: Portrait of Sir Thomas Baring, 2nd Baronet
result.creator: George Engleheart (British, 1752–1829)
description: Portrait of Sir Thomas Baring, 2nd Baronet, 1803. George Engleheart (British, 1752–1829). Watercolor on ivory in a gilt metal frame with plaited brown hair in glazed reserve on back; framed: 8.6 x 7 cm (3 3/8 x 2 3/4 in.); unframed: 8 x 6.3 cm (3 1/8 x 2 1/2 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1942.1140
Engleheart also painted miniatures of Baring's wife and elder sons whose names are listed in the artists fee book; he was charging from 12 to 15 guineas for a miniature painting.

Though this portrait has had the title “Portrait of a Man” since 1942 when it entered the museum’s collection, the sitter was identified by previous owners, including Leo Schidlof and Edward Greene, as a member of the famous Baring banking family, of whom G. C. Williamson mentions several members in his biography of George Engleheart. Thomas Baring (1772–1848) was not elevated to the baronetcy until 1810. Thomas was a member of Parliament, partner in the firm Baring Brothers & Co. from 1804, and chairman of the London and Southwestern Railroad from 1832 to 1833. Baring Brothers & Co. brokered the $15 million Louisiana Purchase in 1802, which doubled the size of the United States and financially refueled Napoleon’s war effort. Thomas wears a dark blue coat with brass buttons, white waistcoat with a high white collar, bow, and frill down the front, all of which was standard attire for British gentlemen at the turn of the century. His hair is worn à l’antique (hair cut short and worn in curls, especially around the forehead), a style sported by men after the turn of the century that evokes the coiffures of statesmen of ancient Rome. The back of the frame contains plaited brown hair. There is a small area of pigment loss located at the lower right edge of the sitter’s coat.

result.title: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack
result.creator: John I Smart (British, 1741–1811)
description: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack, c. 1776. John I Smart (British, 1741–1811). Graphite and wash on laid paper in a modern gold frame; framed: 6.2 x 5.3 cm (2 7/16 x 2 1/16 in.); unframed: 5.8 x 4.8 cm (2 5/16 x 1 7/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1942.1155
Sketches helped John Smart work out the particulars of a portrait before commencing the miniature on ivory, and they were useful in the event that a duplicate might later be required.

Although it is impossible to say if it was always part of the artist’s process to execute a preparatory sketch prior to painting each miniature, we do know that John Smart retained many hundreds of these sketches. A group of preparatory sketches—of which this portrait is one—descended through the Smirke family after Smart’s daughter Sarah gave a sketchbook containing preparatory portrait studies to her friend Mary Smirke, sister of the celebrated Victorian architect Sydney Smirke. This book was probably broken up around 1877 when it was divided between Sydney’s daughters Mary Jemmett and Mrs. Lange, whose portions were both sold at auction in 1928. Compared to his contemporaries George Engleheart (1752–1829) and Andrew Plimer (1763–1837), whose female sitters were often painted in similar simple white gowns, Smart often lavished more attention on the costumes in his portraits of women, whose dresses incorporated colored silks, printed fabrics, and luxury trimmings like lace and fur, as seen in this portrait. Mrs. Bailey wears a violet surcoat trimmed with fur, worn over a cream-colored gown trimmed with a border of alternating pearls and blue stones and two vertical rows of pearls with one large pearl between them. Her brown hair is dressed high with ringlets descending down her neck and over her shoulders. The coiffure is ornamented with a strand of pearls and two ostrich plumes. The case is modern, and there is a brownish cast to what was originally pale, cream-colored paper—the result of light exposure changing the color over time. Smart’s preparatory sketches were compiled in books but once removed were often grouped in frames or placed in lockets such as this one. This portrait was part of the Smirke collection owned by Mary Jemmett, who sold it at Christie’s, London, on February 29, 1928. Lot 61 for this sale is described as “Mrs. Bailey, wearing pale mauve and white dress, her hair dressed high and trimmed with feathers.” The sitter, Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey (née Lamack), of Clapham, married the member of Parliament for Abingdon on March 18, 1773. Her husband was of sufficient means and is recorded in 1775 as having performed his annual distribution of £100 of bread and meat to the poor of his borough. Little else is known about this sitter. This drawing was a preparatory study for a portrait on ivory, signed and dated 1776, and measuring 2 inches high. The ivory miniature was formerly in the Ashcroft collection and was sold at Sotheby’s, London, in May 1946 to Arthur Jaffé, having previously been on loan to the Victoria and Albert Museum from 1924 to 1939. In this sale the miniature is described as “An Attractive Miniature of a Lady, by John Smart, signed and dated 1776, head and gaze three-quarters dexter, a white feather and pearls in her high piled chestnut hair, ringlets falling to the shoulders, wearing a pearl and emerald bordered low-cut cream dress and fur trimmed lavender jacket.” It most recently sold at Christie’s, London, in 2003. This portrait miniature is identical to the preparatory sketch here, both of which describe the sitter as wearing a faintly violet costume, though this color is no longer discernible in the sketch. The current location of the miniature on ivory is unknown. Edward Greene donated this and nine other preparatory studies by Smart to the Cleveland Museum of Art in 1941 and 1942. This sketch was acquired by Greene from Leopold Davis for around $260 in 1930. Although this portrait was probably part of the same sketchbook as the other nine purchased by Greene, Davis did not indicate whether or not this was indeed the case. The majority of these sketches were in a compromised condition, with fading and foxing especially prevalent.

result.title: Shades of Greene : one generation of an English family
result.creator: Lewis, Jeremy
description: xii, 575 pages, 16 unnumbered pages of plates : 20 cm

"Graham Greene was one of the great writers of the last century, as well as enjoying a varied and adventurous career as a secret agent, traveller, publisher and man of letters: but he was not the only member of the Greene family to lead an extraordinary life. Of the twelve children born to brothers Charles and Edward Greene, eight recorded remarkable achievements - from a BBC Director General to an Everest mountaineer, from a female MI6 agent to a champion of Communist China, from a founder of a far-right political party to the inevitable black sheep - and in documenting the interlacing lives of this generation, Lewis provides both a fascinating exercise in group biography and a masterly account of English society in the twentieth century."--Back cover
Originally published: London: Jonathan Cape, 2010
Includes bibliographical references and index

result.title: Portrait of a Woman, called Mrs. Close
result.creator: Horace Hone (British, 1756–1825)
description: Portrait of a Woman, called Mrs. Close, 1786. Horace Hone (British, 1756–1825). Watercolor on ivory in an ormolu frame; framed: 8.9 x 7.5 cm (3 1/2 x 2 15/16 in.); sight: 6.5 x 5.2 cm (2 9/16 x 2 1/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1943.644
The artist, Horace Hone, signed the miniature in the lower right with the monogram HH.

The sitter of this portrait has been called “Mrs. Close” at least from 1929, when Edward Greene purchased the miniature from the dealer Leo Schidlof. The reason for this identification is, however, unknown, as there is no inscribed reference to Mrs. Close on the miniature or any of its supporting materials. Like so many of Horace Hone’s female sitters, her gown and hair are ornamented with strands of pearls, and she is set against an olive green background. Her brown, curly hair falls over her shoulders, dressed high with a pearl ornament on the right side. She has large, dark brown eyes and rosy cheeks and wears a plum-colored dress with a lace fichu around the neckline. The sitter also dons a miniature with the portrait turned toward her chest, exposing the back, which is ornamented with plaited hair. It is noteworthy that the miniature appears this way; even if it had been facing forward, its portrait would not have been legible to the viewer. The decision to place the back foremost underscores the highly private nature of the miniature portrait and its significance for the sitter, who was perhaps accustomed to wearing her miniature with the portrait turned toward her body. This manner of wearing miniatures was adopted by both men and women and was a popular vignette in sentimental novels and poems of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

Her brown hair is dressed high with ringlets descending down her neck and over her shoulders. The coiffure is ornamented with a strand of pearls and two ostrich plumes. The case is modern, and there is a brownish cast to what was originally pale, cream-colored paper—the result of light exposure changing the color over time. Smart’s preparatory sketches were compiled in books but once removed were often grouped in frames or placed in lockets such as this one. This portrait was part of the Smirke collection owned by Mary Jemmett, who sold it at Christie’s, London, on February 29, 1928. Lot 61 for this sale is described as “Mrs. Bailey, wearing pale mauve and white dress, her hair dressed high and trimmed with feathers.” The sitter, Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey (née Lamack), of Clapham, married the member of Parliament for Abingdon on March 18, 1773. Her husband was of sufficient means and is recorded in 1775 as having performed his annual distribution of £100 of bread and meat to the poor of his borough. Little else is known about this sitter. This drawing was a preparatory study for a portrait on ivory, signed and dated 1776, and measuring 2 inches high. The ivory miniature was formerly in the Ashcroft collection and was sold at Sotheby’s, London, in May 1946 to Arthur Jaffé, having previously been on loan to the Victoria and Albert Museum from 1924 to 1939. In this sale the miniature is described as “An Attractive Miniature of a Lady, by John Smart, signed and dated 1776, head and gaze three-quarters dexter, a white feather and pearls in her high piled chestnut hair, ringlets falling to the shoulders, wearing a pearl and emerald bordered low-cut cream dress and fur trimmed lavender jacket.” It most recently sold at Christie’s, London, in 2003. This portrait miniature is identical to the preparatory sketch here, both of which describe the sitter as wearing a faintly violet costume, though this color is no longer discernible in the sketch. The current location of the miniature on ivory is unknown. Edward Greene donated this and nine other preparatory studies by Smart to the Cleveland Museum of Art in 1941 and 1942. This sketch was acquired by Greene from Leopold Davis for around $260 in 1930. Although this portrait was probably part of the same sketchbook as the other nine purchased by Greene, Davis did not indicate whether or not this was indeed the case. The majority of these sketches were in a compromised condition, with fading and foxing especially prevalent.

result.title: DVD Transfer 217 (NBA on NBC: 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals - Chicago Bulls at New York Knicks: Game 7 - Partial Recording)
result.creator: NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast; WEAU-Gray Media
result.description: (c)1994 NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast and WEAU-Gray Media So, this came as a bonus DVD recording alongside Game 7 of the 1990 Eastern Conference Finals I posted a while back. However, I had a much more difficult time ripping the video for this one (and had actually given up on this one not that long ago) before deciding to give it one more try last week. DVD Transfer 217 contains a mostly-complete (unfortunately, it appears that the original recorder's tape ran out with a few minutes left in the game) recording of Game 7 of the 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals involving the biggest rivalry of the early 1990s between the three-time defending NBA champion Chicago Bulls (55-27 and the #3 seed) and the Atlantic Division champion New York Knicks (tied with the Central Division champion Atlanta Hawks for the Eastern Conference's best record at 57-25). Entering the 1993-94 season; the Knicks (who had no draft picks in 1993 after their lone pick was traded to Orlando) had faced the Bulls in the post-season in each of the three previous playoffs and had been eliminated each time (including the 1992 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals where the series went the full 7 games before Chicago advanced and the 1993 Eastern Conference Finals where the Knicks - with the conference's best record - were eliminated in 6 games) and were seeking their first trip to the Finals since 1973. Changes to the Pat Riley-led Knicks included the off-season arrival of Sacramento Kings forward Anthony Bonner and a mid-season trade that saw the Knicks trade guard Tony Campbell and their 1st round pick in 1997 to the lowly Dallas Mavericks in exchange for point guard Derek Harper (picked up after starting point guard Doc Rivers suffered a season-ending knee injury early in the year); while late in the regular-season longtime owner Paramount sold both the team and the Madison Square Garden arena to Viacom (which eventually sold the team to a consortium of ITT and Cablevision; with Cablevision currently being the sole owner), advancing to this series by ousting the (then-)New Jersey Nets 3-1 in the first round. Meanwhile; the Chicago Bulls entered the 1993-94 season seeking to become the first team in any professional sport since the Boston Celtics of the 1960s to win a 4th consecutive championship (the Celtics winning 8 consecutive NBA titles between 1959-66) but just before the season were rocked by the sudden retirement of Michael Jordan just over two months after the July 23, 1993 murder of his father James (whose body wasn't discovered until 10 days later, with the assailants - Daniel Green and Larry Martin Demery - eventually being convicted and sentenced to life in prison), eventually deciding to try his hand at baseball with the Birmingham Barons, a minor-league team affiliated with the Chicago White Sox (incidentally also owned by Bulls owner Jerry Reinsdorf). Other changes to the Bulls roster included the drafting of rookie forward Corie Blount along with the signing of journeyman shooting guard Pete Myers (Myers, who replaced Jordan at shooting guard, had most recently played in Italy), former Sacramento Kings center (but having also most recently played in Italy) Bill Wennington and point guard Steve Kerr (late of the Orlando Magic) as well as Croatian forward Toni Kukoc (who the Bulls had drafted in 1990) making his NBA debut while during the season backup center Stacey King was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for Australian-born center Luc Longley. The Bulls entered the playoffs with a 3-0 sweep of frequent post-season rival Cleveland Cavaliers (the 3rd and final game being the last game played at Richfield Coliseum before the Cavs moved to Gund Arena {now Rocket Arena}). This would be a closely-fought series (with the home team emerging victorious in each game) that included Kukoc making the game-winning 23-foot buzzer-beater shot in Game 3 for a 104-102 Bulls win to make the series 2-1 (Kukoc's shot being made possible in part after Scottie Pippen - who replaced Jordan as the Bulls' main offensive threat - refused to enter the game due to being upset with Phil Jackson drawing up the last play of the game for Kukoc while Pippen would inbound; that game also included a fight between Derek Harper and Bulls guard Jo Jo English that spilled into the stands - with NBA Commissioner David Stern in attendance); an 87-86 Knicks victory in Game 5 noted by a questionable call by Hue Hollins, who determined that Pippen had fouled Knicks guard Hubert Davis, who sank both free throws for what proved the winning points and a Game 6 Chicago victory at Chicago Stadium 93-79 (the biggest margin of victory for either team in the series) noted for Pippen dunking on Knicks center Patrick Ewing. Game 7 would be a closely fought battle with the Knicks leading 22-19 at the end of the 1st, 38-37 at halftime and 67-63 at the end of the 3rd quarter before pulling away in the fourth to dethrone the three-time defending NBA champion Bulls 87-77. Calling the action for NBC are - as per usual - Marv Albert (who when he wasn't on the clock for NBC was also working games for the Knicks on the MSG cable network) and former Orlando Magic head coach Matt Goukas (who left shortly after the 1993 draft) and sideline reporter Ahmad Rashad; while NBA Showtime host Bob Costas hosted NBC's coverage (which including an airing of the 1994 NBA Draft Lottery during halftime) NOTES 1. For the Bulls, Scottie Pippen led the team with 20 points, 5 assists and 16 rebounds (albeit with 3 turnovers and making only 8 of his 22 field goal attempts), while Horace Grant added 17 points and 4 boards (but also 5 fouls), Pete Myers adding 15 points and 4 rebounds (and also 4 fouls); with the only significant reserve support coming from Toni Kukoc (9 points, 4 rebounds). 2. For the Knicks; four of their starters finished in double figures in points (the exception being point guard Derek Harper with 6 points). Patrick Ewing led the way with 18 points, 17 rebounds, 6 assists and a block; while Charles Oakley (who began his career with the Bulls before moving to the Big Apple in 1988 in a trade with Bill Cartwright) added 17 points and a game-high 20 rebounds. John Starks added 10 points and 3 assists (though shooting an abysmal 2-for-11) while Charles Smith (whose claim to NBA notoriety was his having a potential game-winning shot blocked 4 times in Game 5 of the previous year's Eastern Conference Finals) added 11 points and 2 blocks. Bench support came from Anthony Mason (9 points, 5 rebounds), Hubert Davis (8 points) and Greg Anthony (7 points). 3. The Bulls' defeat meant that Game 6 was the final game played at Chicago Stadium, with both the Bulls and the NHL's Chicago Blackhawks both moving across the street to the United Center (where they remain as of 2025) and the old stadium being torn down between February and May 1995. 4. The Bulls' defeat also marked the final game with Chicago for a number of players connected to their (first) three-peat, including center Bill Cartwright (dealt to Seattle for his final season), power forward Horace Grant (who jumped ship to the rapidly improving Magic), center Scott Williams (who left for the lowly Philadelphia 76ers), guard Jo Jo English (who went to the CBA's Pittsburgh Piranhas) and point guard John Paxson (Paxson - who missed most of the season due to injury - announced his retirement soon after) 5. As for the Knicks, they found themselves facing a surprising strong challenge in the Eastern Conference Finals from the Indiana Pacers, who pushed New York the full 7 once again (including a Game 5 93-86 Pacers victory remembered for Reggie Miller scoring 25 points in the 4th quarter) before the Knicks emerged victorious with a 94-90 victory in Game 7 (remembered for Patrick Ewing making the game-clinching dunk with 26.9 seconds left to play). That set up an NBA Finals match with the Houston Rockets (seeking not just their first NBA title {having lost to the Celtics in both 1981 and 1986} but also to remove the legacy of the city's sports teams as choke artists {first with the NFL's Houston Oilers blowing leads in three consecutive playoff games - most infamously blowing a 35-3 lead early in the 3rd quarter in the 1992 AFC Wild-Card Game to the Buffalo Bills, who won 41-38 in overtime in what became known as "The Comeback" - as well as the Rockets falling behind 0-2 to the Phoenix Suns in the Western Conference Semi-Finals that led to the Houston Chronicle's "Choke City" headline before rallying to win that series in 7 games and leading to the "Clutch City" nickname}). That series would also go the full 7 (meaning that, since the first round was a Best-of-5 at the time, had the Nets won one more game against the Knicks in their first round meeting, New York would have played a maximum of 26 playoff games) - with the Knicks leading 3-2 after their 91-84 win in Game 5 on June 17 (a game overshadowed by the O.J. Simpson chase in which the former Buffalo Bills legend and NBC sportscaster was involved in a chase - in a white Ford Bronco owned by Simpson's one-time Bills teammate Al Cowlings - with the L.A.P.D. after Simpson was charged with the murders of estranged wife Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman before the Juice surrendered; eventually being acquitted {though later held liable in civil court} following a trial that was less a criminal trial and more a media circus) before the Rockets - seeking their first title in a still-existing league (the city's most recent championship being the Houston Aeros in 1975 with the old World Hockey Association) - won their last 2 games (including a 86-84 win in Game 6 which saw Rockets center Hakeem Olajuwon blocking a potential game-winning 3-pointer by John Starks; with a rattled Starks making only 2 of 18 shots in the deciding Game 7) to clinch their first NBA championship (and in the process denying New York City a chance to celebrate both an NBA and NHL championship, as between Games 3 and 4 of the NBA Finals the New York Rangers won their first Stanley Cup since 1940 as well as making Knicks head coach Pat Riley the only coach to lose 2 Game 7's in the NBA Finals with different teams {the first being when Riley's Lakers were defeated by the Celtics in Game 7 of the 1984 NBA Finals; while had the Knicks won Game 7 he would have been the first coach to win 2 Game 7's in the Finals with different teams - the first would have been with the Lakers in Game 7 in 1988})

result.title: Is There Scale-Dependent Bias in Single-Field Inflation?
creator: Roland de Putter
Olivier Doré
Daniel Green
result.description: Scale-dependent halo bias due to local primordial non-Gaussianity provides a strong test of single-field inflation. While it is universally understood that single-field inflation predicts negligible scale-dependent bias compared to current observational uncertainties, there is still disagreement on the exact level of scale-dependent bias at a level that could strongly impact inferences made from future surveys. In this paper, we clarify this confusion and derive in various ways that there is exactly zero scale-dependent bias in single-field inflation. Much of the current confusion follows from the fact that single-field inflation does predict a mode coupling of matter perturbations at the level of $f_{NL}^{loc} \approx -5/3$, which naively would lead to scale-dependent bias. However, we show explicitly that this mode coupling cancels out when perturbations are evaluated at a fixed physical scale rather than fixed coordinate scale. Furthermore, we show how the absence of scale-dependent bias can be derived easily in any gauge. This result can then be incorporated into a complete description of the observed galaxy clustering, including the previously studied general relativistic terms, which are important at the same level as scale-dependent bias of order $f_{NL}^{loc} \sim 1$. This description will allow us to draw unbiased conclusions about inflation from future galaxy clustering data.

result.title: Testing Split Supersymmetry with Inflation
creator: Nathaniel Craig
Daniel Green
result.description: Split supersymmetry (SUSY) -- in which SUSY is relevant to our universe but largely inaccessible at current accelerators -- has become increasingly plausible given the absence of new physics at the LHC, the success of gauge coupling unification, and the observed Higgs mass. Indirect probes of split SUSY such as electric dipole moments (EDMs) and flavor violation offer hope for further evidence but are ultimately limited in their reach. Inflation offers an alternate window into SUSY through the direct production of superpartners during inflation. These particles are capable of leaving imprints in future cosmological probes of primordial non-gaussianity. Given the recent observations of BICEP2, the scale of inflation is likely high enough to probe the full range of split SUSY scenarios and therefore offers a unique advantage over low energy probes. The key observable for future experiments is equilateral non-gaussianity, which will be probed by both cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large scale structure (LSS) surveys. In the event of a detection, we forecast our ability to find evidence for superpartners through the scaling behavior in the squeezed limit of the bispectrum.

result.title: Reheating Closed String Inflation
result.creator: Daniel Green
result.description: Protecting the inflationary potential from quantum corrections typically requires symmetries that constrain the form of couplings of the inflaton to other sectors. We will explore how these restrictions affect reheating in models with UV completions. In particular, we look at how reheating occurs when inflation is governed by closed strings, using N-flation as an example. We find that coupling the inflaton preferentially to the Standard Model is difficult, and hidden sectors are typically reheated. Observational constraints are only met by a fraction of the models. In some working models, relativistic relics in the hidden sector provide dark matter candidates with masses that range from keV to PeV, with lighter masses being preferred.

result.title: A New Target for Cosmic Axion Searches
creator: Daniel Baumann
Daniel Green
Benjamin Wallisch
result.description: Future CMB experiments have the potential to probe the density of relativistic species at the sub-percent level. Sensitivity at this level allows light thermal relics to be detected up to arbitrarily high decoupling temperatures. Conversely, the absence of a detection would require extra light species never to have been in equilibrium with the Standard Model. In this paper, we exploit this feature to demonstrate the sensitivity of future cosmological observations to the couplings of axions to all of the Standard Model degrees of freedom. In many cases, the constraints achievable from cosmology will surpass existing bounds from laboratory experiments and astrophysical observations by orders of magnitude.

result.title: Difficulties with Recollapsing models in Closed Isotropic Loop Quantum Cosmology
creator: Daniel Green
William G. Unruh
result.description: The use of techniques from loop quantum gravity for cosmological models may solve some difficult problems in quantum cosmology. The solutions under a number of circumstances have been well studied. We will analyse the behaviour of solutions in the closed model, focusing on the behaviour of a universe containing a massless scalar field. The asymptotic behaviour of the solutions is examined, and is used to determine requirements of the initial conditions.

result.title: DVD Transfer 217 (NBA on NBC: 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals - Chicago Bulls at New York Knicks: Game 7 - Partial Recording)
result.creator: NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast; WEAU-Gray Media
result.description: (c)1994 NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast and WEAU-Gray Media So, this came as a bonus DVD recording alongside Game 7 of the 1990 Eastern Conference Finals I posted a while back. However, I had a much more difficult time ripping the video for this one (and had actually given up on this one not that long ago) before deciding to give it one more try last week. DVD Transfer 217 contains a mostly-complete (unfortunately, it appears that the original recorder's tape ran out with a few minutes left in the game) recording of Game 7 of the 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals involving the biggest rivalry of the early 1990s between the three-time defending NBA champion Chicago Bulls (55-27 and the #3 seed) and the Atlantic Division champion New York Knicks (tied with the Central Division champion Atlanta Hawks for the Eastern Conference's best record at 57-25). Entering the 1993-94 season; the Knicks (who had no draft picks in 1993 after their lone pick was traded to Orlando) had faced the Bulls in the post-season in each of the three previous playoffs and had been eliminated each time (including the 1992 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals where the series went the full 7 games before Chicago advanced and the 1993 Eastern Conference Finals where the Knicks - with the conference's best record - were eliminated in 6 games) and were seeking their first trip to the Finals since 1973. Changes to the Pat Riley-led Knicks included the off-season arrival of Sacramento Kings forward Anthony Bonner and a mid-season trade that saw the Knicks trade guard Tony Campbell and their 1st round pick in 1997 to the lowly Dallas Mavericks in exchange for point guard Derek Harper (picked up after starting point guard Doc Rivers suffered a season-ending knee injury early in the year); while late in the regular-season longtime owner Paramount sold both the team and the Madison Square Garden arena to Viacom (which eventually sold the team to a consortium of ITT and Cablevision; with Cablevision currently being the sole owner), advancing to this series by ousting the (then-)New Jersey Nets 3-1 in the first round. Meanwhile; the Chicago Bulls entered the 1993-94 season seeking to become the first team in any professional sport since the Boston Celtics of the 1960s to win a 4th consecutive championship (the Celtics winning 8 consecutive NBA titles between 1959-66) but just before the season were rocked by the sudden retirement of Michael Jordan just over two months after the July 23, 1993 murder of his father James (whose body wasn't discovered until 10 days later, with the assailants - Daniel Green and Larry Martin Demery - eventually being convicted and sentenced to life in prison), eventually deciding to try his hand at baseball with the Birmingham Barons, a minor-league team affiliated with the Chicago White Sox (incidentally also owned by Bulls owner Jerry Reinsdorf). Other changes to the Bulls roster included the drafting of rookie forward Corie Blount along with the signing of journeyman shooting guard Pete Myers (Myers, who replaced Jordan at shooting guard, had most recently played in Italy), former Sacramento Kings center (but having also most recently played in Italy) Bill Wennington and point guard Steve Kerr (late of the Orlando Magic) as well as Croatian forward Toni Kukoc (who the Bulls had drafted in 1990) making his NBA debut while during the season backup center Stacey King was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for Australian-born center Luc Longley. The Bulls entered the playoffs with a 3-0 sweep of frequent post-season rival Cleveland Cavaliers (the 3rd and final game being the last game played at Richfield Coliseum before the Cavs moved to Gund Arena {now Rocket Arena}). This would be a closely-fought series (with the home team emerging victorious in each game) that included Kukoc making the game-winning 23-foot buzzer-beater shot in Game 3 for a 104-102 Bulls win to make the series 2-1 (Kukoc's shot being made possible in part after Scottie Pippen - who replaced Jordan as the Bulls' main offensive threat - refused to enter the game due to being upset with Phil Jackson drawing up the last play of the game for Kukoc while Pippen would inbound; that game also included a fight between Derek Harper and Bulls guard Jo Jo English that spilled into the stands - with NBA Commissioner David Stern in attendance); an 87-86 Knicks victory in Game 5 noted by a questionable call by Hue Hollins, who determined that Pippen had fouled Knicks guard Hubert Davis, who sank both free throws for what proved the winning points and a Game 6 Chicago victory at Chicago Stadium 93-79 (the biggest margin of victory for either team in the series) noted for Pippen dunking on Knicks center Patrick Ewing. Game 7 would be a closely fought battle with the Knicks leading 22-19 at the end of the 1st, 38-37 at halftime and 67-63 at the end of the 3rd quarter before pulling away in the fourth to dethrone the three-time defending NBA champion Bulls 87-77. Calling the action for NBC are - as per usual - Marv Albert (who when he wasn't on the clock for NBC was also working games for the Knicks on the MSG cable network) and former Orlando Magic head coach Matt Goukas (who left shortly after the 1993 draft) and sideline reporter Ahmad Rashad; while NBA Showtime host Bob Costas hosted NBC's coverage (which including an airing of the 1994 NBA Draft Lottery during halftime) NOTES 1. For the Bulls, Scottie Pippen led the team with 20 points, 5 assists and 16 rebounds (albeit with 3 turnovers and making only 8 of his 22 field goal attempts), while Horace Grant added 17 points and 4 boards (but also 5 fouls), Pete Myers adding 15 points and 4 rebounds (and also 4 fouls); with the only significant reserve support coming from Toni Kukoc (9 points, 4 rebounds). 2. For the Knicks; four of their starters finished in double figures in points (the exception being point guard Derek Harper with 6 points). Patrick Ewing led the way with 18 points, 17 rebounds, 6 assists and a block; while Charles Oakley (who began his career with the Bulls before moving to the Big Apple in 1988 in a trade with Bill Cartwright) added 17 points and a game-high 20 rebounds. John Starks added 10 points and 3 assists (though shooting an abysmal 2-for-11) while Charles Smith (whose claim to NBA notoriety was his having a potential game-winning shot blocked 4 times in Game 5 of the previous year's Eastern Conference Finals) added 11 points and 2 blocks. Bench support came from Anthony Mason (9 points, 5 rebounds), Hubert Davis (8 points) and Greg Anthony (7 points). 3. The Bulls' defeat meant that Game 6 was the final game played at Chicago Stadium, with both the Bulls and the NHL's Chicago Blackhawks both moving across the street to the United Center (where they remain as of 2025) and the old stadium being torn down between February and May 1995. 4. The Bulls' defeat also marked the final game with Chicago for a number of players connected to their (first) three-peat, including center Bill Cartwright (dealt to Seattle for his final season), power forward Horace Grant (who jumped ship to the rapidly improving Magic), center Scott Williams (who left for the lowly Philadelphia 76ers), guard Jo Jo English (who went to the CBA's Pittsburgh Piranhas) and point guard John Paxson (Paxson - who missed most of the season due to injury - announced his retirement soon after) 5. As for the Knicks, they found themselves facing a surprising strong challenge in the Eastern Conference Finals from the Indiana Pacers, who pushed New York the full 7 once again (including a Game 5 93-86 Pacers victory remembered for Reggie Miller scoring 25 points in the 4th quarter) before the Knicks emerged victorious with a 94-90 victory in Game 7 (remembered for Patrick Ewing making the game-clinching dunk with 26.9 seconds left to play). That set up an NBA Finals match with the Houston Rockets (seeking not just their first NBA title {having lost to the Celtics in both 1981 and 1986} but also to remove the legacy of the city's sports teams as choke artists {first with the NFL's Houston Oilers blowing leads in three consecutive playoff games - most infamously blowing a 35-3 lead early in the 3rd quarter in the 1992 AFC Wild-Card Game to the Buffalo Bills, who won 41-38 in overtime in what became known as "The Comeback" - as well as the Rockets falling behind 0-2 to the Phoenix Suns in the Western Conference Semi-Finals that led to the Houston Chronicle's "Choke City" headline before rallying to win that series in 7 games and leading to the "Clutch City" nickname}). That series would also go the full 7 (meaning that, since the first round was a Best-of-5 at the time, had the Nets won one more game against the Knicks in their first round meeting, New York would have played a maximum of 26 playoff games) - with the Knicks leading 3-2 after their 91-84 win in Game 5 on June 17 (a game overshadowed by the O.J. Simpson chase in which the former Buffalo Bills legend and NBC sportscaster was involved in a chase - in a white Ford Bronco owned by Simpson's one-time Bills teammate Al Cowlings - with the L.A.P.D. after Simpson was charged with the murders of estranged wife Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman before the Juice surrendered; eventually being acquitted {though later held liable in civil court} following a trial that was less a criminal trial and more a media circus) before the Rockets - seeking their first title in a still-existing league (the city's most recent championship being the Houston Aeros in 1975 with the old World Hockey Association) - won their last 2 games (including a 86-84 win in Game 6 which saw Rockets center Hakeem Olajuwon blocking a potential game-winning 3-pointer by John Starks; with a rattled Starks making only 2 of 18 shots in the deciding Game 7) to clinch their first NBA championship (and in the process denying New York City a chance to celebrate both an NBA and NHL championship, as between Games 3 and 4 of the NBA Finals the New York Rangers won their first Stanley Cup since 1940 as well as making Knicks head coach Pat Riley the only coach to lose 2 Game 7's in the NBA Finals with different teams {the first being when Riley's Lakers were defeated by the Celtics in Game 7 of the 1984 NBA Finals; while had the Knicks won Game 7 he would have been the first coach to win 2 Game 7's in the Finals with different teams - the first would have been with the Lakers in Game 7 in 1988})

result.title: SpaceWarZ
result.description: "SpaceWarZ is a two-player game. Each player tries to destroy the other player's ship, without getting his own ship destroyed. If you destroy the other player's ship, your score goes up by one; the first player to reach the agreed-upon high score wins the game. Ships can rotate and they can accelerate by using their engines. If the gravity option is being used, then ships can also move by being attracted to the sun (or black hole, if it is present). The game tries to realistically simulate motion, such that if you accelerate forwards for five seconds, its going to take another five seconds of acceleration in the opposite direction to stop your motion. Each ship can fire bullets. Each player can have up to five bullets in action at once. Bullets travel for approximately 2/3 of the horizontal length of the window before they self-destruct. A ship can be destroyed by being hit by a bullet (even by one of your own bullets!), by being sucked into the sun or a black hole, or by ramming into the other player's ship."

result.title: Dr. Dan Green on Mental Health and Leading Men Well
result.creator: International Church of Monrovia
result.description: Today on the No Regrets Podcast, Nate Gruber is joined by Dr. Dan Green, Clinical Director of New Life Resources and a long-time partner of No Regrets, for an important conversation on the mental health of the men we lead—and the men we are becoming. Dr. Green brings practical insight for leaders who feel stuck or are facing roadblocks in their own lives or on their teams. As mental health becomes more widely discussed, many men are still unsure what to do with what they're feeling. Labels can sometimes increase isolation rather than bring clarity, especially when men struggle to express their needs. Nate and Dan explore the reality that men today are often more psychologically drained than physically exhausted—and more disconnected than ever. In a world filled with constant information, they emphasize the importance of real, face-to-face connection and intentional relationships. Every man carries a unique story and set of pressures, and understanding those demands is key to leading well. They also discuss how leaders must first care for their own health before they can care for others. As Dr. Green shares, every man needs a few trusted relationships—men who aren't impressed by him, but who will challenge, support, and walk with him honestly. When leaders model vulnerability and authenticity, they create space for others to do the same. This episode offers practical tools for understanding your own needs, recognizing what's being blocked when frustration arises, and learning how to lead with greater awareness, care, and connection. Ultimately, as we grow in knowing God, we begin to understand ourselves more fully—and lead others more effectively. Resource Mentioned: Overcoming Guilt and Shame by Daniel Green and Mel Lawrenz

result.description: Today on the No Regrets Podcast, Nate Gruber is joined by Dr. Dan Green, Clinical Director of New Life Resources and a long-time partner of No Regrets, for an important conversation on the mental health of the men we lead—and the men we are becoming. Dr. Green brings practical insight for leaders who feel stuck or are facing roadblocks in their own lives or on their teams. As mental health becomes more widely discussed, many men are still unsure what to do with what they're feeling. Labels can sometimes increase isolation rather than bring clarity, especially when men struggle to express their needs. Nate and Dan explore the reality that men today are often more psychologically drained than physically exhausted—and more disconnected than ever. In a world filled with constant information, they emphasize the importance of real, face-to-face connection and intentional relationships. Every man carries a unique story and set of pressures, and understanding those demands is key to leading well. They also discuss how leaders must first care for their own health before they can care for others. As Dr. Green shares, every man needs a few trusted relationships—men who aren't impressed by him, but who will challenge, support, and walk with him honestly. When leaders model vulnerability and authenticity, they create space for others to do the same. This episode offers practical tools for understanding your own needs, recognizing what's being blocked when frustration arises, and learning how to lead with greater awareness, care, and connection. Ultimately, as we grow in knowing God, we begin to understand ourselves more fully—and lead others more effectively. Resource Mentioned: Overcoming Guilt and Shame by Daniel Green and Mel Lawrenz

result.title: Greening Out 29
result.creator: Daniel Greene & Caitlin Greene
result.description: Caity and Dan finally get round to doing a show based around Lewis Carroll's classic 1865 kids book "Alice's Adventures In Wonderland". We start by explaining why Caity is so excited about this show and her slight obsession with collecting copies of said book. We talk about the weird and surreal scenes in the book and probably read way to much into it. We bring up themes of logic, Buddhism, reincarnation, good vs. bad self-help, child abuse, morality, leaving people alone and wanting to be left alone in life. We talk about time and a couple of different theories about it found in religion, Caity's view of time, saying what you mean and thinking before you speak. The movie Labyrinth, David Bowie and why the powerful pro-Labyrinth lobby will get Dan one day. We get into Alice's identity issues and why she is obsessed with he concept of who she is. Caity's theories about how the be-headings ordered by the Red Queen may mean something else and other people's theories about Lewis Carroll's sexuality in regards to young girls. We come to the conclusion that despite her issues Alice is a bad-ass who constantly questions authority figures in the book and we salute her for it.

result.title: Greening Out Podcast #25 - Caity and Dan Try To Solve The Mystery of Scotland's Socialist Tendencies
result.creator: Daniel Greene/ Caitlin Greene
result.description: Caity and Dan present their ideas as to why so many people in Scotland have socialist tendencies, we chat about Margaret Thatcher, the poll tax (why Murray Rothbard thought that Thatcher had missed the point of a flat tax) and how future Scottish socialist politicians got their start during the poll tax riots, the bedroom tax, Red Clydeside, Jimmy Reid and his communist party education and of course Dan's weird Alan Partridge ring-tones. We go on to explore how these ideas from the past continue to be mainstream in younger people because of indoctrination by their parents, the high number of state employees in Scotland compared to England, the privatisation of Royal Mail, the more state spending per-head in Scotland in comparison with England, our definition of socialism, the problems with debating and why Dan can't be arsed with it, Scottish movies and TV shows and why a lot of them show very poor and gritty conditions. We then lighten up with funny Irn Bru adverts and how they offended people, the notion of a voluntary NHS, politically acceptable radicals and what real radicals are and what markets want. We question what the Labour party are even for anymore, how politicians aren't real people and why it's ridiculous that many of them have never had a real job, the questionable ethics of said politicians, Tony Blair and the Iraq war, how anarchism used to be a much larger movement in the early 20 th  century, the work of Voltairine De Cleyre, the apathy present in modern culture and our optimism of the power of the internet to spread libertarian and anarchist ideas widely. We finish with the punk band The Exploited's song "Don't Pay The Poll Tax" .

result.title: Greening Out Interview #19 - Bill Buppert on Revolution
result.creator: Daniel Greene
result.description: Caity and Dan Welcome Bill Buppert back to the show for a very interesting conversation based around the topic of revolution! Bill is a retired Army officer who has written and spoken widely on the issues of freedom and liberty. He is the Founder and Publisher of ZeroGov.com where he publishes essays twice weekly. The abolitionist author of ZeroGov: Limited Government, Unicorns and other Mythological Creatures, he lives with his family in the American SW in the high desert. Bill is working on two books this year: a novel and a book examining all of Lysander Spooner's collected works. He is an acknowledged expert on irregular warfare and revolutionary movements. We chat about violent vs. non-violent revolutions and where a violent one may end up nowadays. Ireland - from the 1916 Easter Rising to the civil war of the 1920's to the troubles that later followed, Michael Collins, Eamon De Valera, Che Guevara, the Soviet Union and the problems with socialists fighting socialists. We also get into the American revolution, why violence doesn't work, Russell Brand, John and Bobby Kennedy, etymology, the importance of discrimination in straight thinking, anarchism and abolitionism, the examined life and why it's important, government control, psychopaths in politics, western interventionism in the Middle East, anarcho-communism, the war for the mind, the influence of mainstream media and more.

result.title: Greening Out Podcast #26 - Bad Capitalism Can Lead To Socialism
result.creator: Daniel Greene /Caitlin Greene
result.description: Join Caity and Dan for one of our more hardcore libertarian/anarchist podcasts, we start by complaining about their internet going down for a few days in the Greening Out household then get on to how bad customer service can be very frustrating and can lead to some people thinking that certain industries would work better if they were nationalised. We talk about why nationalisation doesn't work, how the government has no incentive to give any kind of customer service, people talking romantically about the 1970's in the UK, some modern examples of political parties who are pushing for certain industries to be nationalised, government taking 'payment holidays' from pension funds and why government departments and industries don't care how much you complain. We go on to chat about how government can't even finish painting a bridge in Glasgow, why local councils do so-called public works that are unnecessary  just to obtain the same budget the year after, we then go on the do a little 'ancapistan' private road theorizing and Caity tells us about government roads that stink of urine. We theorize further about why private parks could also be preferable to government parks, why some people get the wrong idea about the free market, 'satanic' messages in music, Caity's 'Hixian' views.  The Scottish Socialist Party and their crazy economic ideas, the problems with socialism in general, Austrian economics and the subjective theory of value, tax evasion in all it's forms and why it is not a bad thing because you owe the state nothing. We go on to talk about feeling like a libertarian instinctively, Dan's journey from socialism to libertarianism, Penn & Teller and card magic and Walter Block. We get into anarchism it's relation to belief in god and finish by mentioning (again) Libertarians Against Humanity.

result.title: Mark Weber, Interview avec Jim Rizoli 2016
result.creator: didi18
result.description: Nous exigeons la vérité ! Mark Weber et David Irving retournent leur veste... 1 - [Jürgen Graf a complètement démonté les élucubrations de David Irving sur ces prétendus gazages. Voy. « David Irving et les “camps de l’Aktion Reinhardt“ », avril 2009.] 2. [voir. en bas la très importante réaction de Fred Leuchter lui-même.]. 3. [voir. R. Faurisson, « Treblinka : un guide exceptionnel », 12 oct. 2003 qui est le récit de la visite faite en juin-juillet 1986 par le Professeur au « camp d’extermination » de Treblinka.] 4. À la suite de cette interview nous avons reçu le message suivant de Fred Leuchter le 15 février 2016 : En dépit des preuves que possèdent Irving et Weber concernant les « limited gassings » [gazages limités] il n’en reste pas moins que les exécutions massives par gaz sont impossibles d’un point de vue matériel. Les preuves citées par Weber et Irving sont des indices de preuves (« circumstantial evidence »). J’ai le plus grand respect pour les indices de preuves. Ils indiquent qu’il faut poursuivre les recherches. Ces preuves convaincront les uns et ne convaincront pas les autres et je peux respecter l’opinion de chacun. Cependant, le fait qu’il est impossible d’un point de vue mécanique d’effectuer des exécutions de masse au gaz n’est pas un indice de preuve. C’est un fait scientifique/mécanique. Ceci devrait balayer tous les doutes créés sur ce sujet dans l’esprit de chacun. Si on est parfois prêt à croire « Leuchter » et « Rudolf », on devrait les croire tout le temps : il n’y a pas de position intermédiaire dans la science (Rudolf) ni dans la mécanique (Leuchter). Noir c’est noir et blanc c’est blanc. Nous n’avons pas de gris. Pas question pour moi d’avoir des doutes. Idem pour Germar. Fred Leuchter.

result.title: Greening Out 29
result.creator: Daniel Greene & Caitlin Greene
result.description: Caity and Dan finally get round to doing a show based around Lewis Carroll's classic 1865 kids book "Alice's Adventures In Wonderland". We start by explaining why Caity is so excited about this show and her slight obsession with collecting copies of said book. We talk about the weird and surreal scenes in the book and probably read way to much into it. We bring up themes of logic, Buddhism, reincarnation, good vs. bad self-help, child abuse, morality, leaving people alone and wanting to be left alone in life. We talk about time and a couple of different theories about it found in religion, Caity's view of time, saying what you mean and thinking before you speak. The movie Labyrinth, David Bowie and why the powerful pro-Labyrinth lobby will get Dan one day. We get into Alice's identity issues and why she is obsessed with he concept of who she is. Caity's theories about how the be-headings ordered by the Red Queen may mean something else and other people's theories about Lewis Carroll's sexuality in regards to young girls. We come to the conclusion that despite her issues Alice is a bad-ass who constantly questions authority figures in the book and we salute her for it.

result.title: The Leuchter Report
result.creator: Dr. Fred Leuchter,Ernst Zündel
result.description: The Leuchter report is a document authored by American execution technician Fred A. Leuchter, who was commissioned by Ernst Zündel to defend him at his trial in Canada for distributing Holocaust denial material. Leuchter compiled the report in 1988 with the intention of investigating the feasibility of mass homicidal gassings at Nazi extermination camps, specifically at Auschwitz. He travelled to the camp, collected multiple pieces of brick from the remains of the crematoria and gas chambers ,brought them back to the United States, and submitted them for chemical analysis.  Dr. Fred Leuchter is the only American with the expertise to accurately design, build and critique execution equipment for the various states in the union that condemn people to death. Because of his experience, he was called upon to travel to the death camps in Western Germany to examine if people were actually put to death in concentration camps, and this report was submitted as evidence at the Canadian free-speech trial where Ernst Zundel was being charges with thought crimes. This report contains numerous tables, figures, photos and charts and concludes with the expert opinion that âIt is the best engineering opinion of this author that the alleged gas chambers at the inspected sites could not have then been, or now, be utilized or seriously considered to function as execution gas chambers.â This report is the final nail in the coffin of the holo-hoax myth.

WARREN DIRECTOR OF ADMINISTRATION J. M. WRAY, JR. DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS W. L. BRITTLE, JR. DIRECTOR OF ENGINEERING OSCAR K. MABRY DI-ECTOR OF PLANNING H. W. WORRALL DIRECTOR OF FINANCIAL AFFAIRS IN REPLY PLEASE REFER TO P.O. Box 429 Fairfax, Virginia 22030-0629 This is in reference to the road improvements needed to accommodate the planned expansion of the CIA Headquarters at McLean. Additional analysis by the Virginia Department of Highways and Transportation confirms the need for grade separations at the intersection of Routes 123 and 193 and the CIA entrance. A turning movement study by the Virginia Department of Highways and Trans- portation indicates peak hour volumes that are 22% greater than the base volumes utilized in the CIA Master Development Plan. The traffic volumes are great enough, at several locations, that acceptable levels of service cannot be obtained with at-grade intersections. Therefore, we are recommending a design with three grade separations: first, where the ramp from eastbound 193 to northbound 123 crosses southbound 123; second, where the ramp from northbound 123 to the CIA entrance crosses southbound 123; third, where the ramp from the CIA entrance to northbound 123 crosses southbound 123. The enclosed sketch, on an aerial mosaic, depicts the type of design that we are proposing. The three bridges can be expected to cost approximately $1 million, based on a figure of $60 per square foot. Grading and paving can be expected to total approximately $1.3 million. These figures are based on our experience with recent contract prices. To cover current inflationary costs, we estimate a total figure of $2.5 million. I hope this provides the information you need to proceed with planning and budgeting for the new facilities. If I may be of further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact me. C. 20505 Reference is made to your letter of September 18 regarding a proposed agree- ment to cover the CIA's funding of an extension of the deceleration lane on northbound 1-495 and the widening of the eastbound Parkway exit ramp. When this subject was first raised in our meeting on May 21, I advised that we would investigate the matter to see if these improvements were needed to improve access to the Parkway ramp. My letter of June 5 pointed out that the a.m, backups on northbound 1-495 are brought about by the lack of traffic capacity on Cabin John Bridge. You indicated in our meeting that your studies had revealed that these improve- ments would improve access to the Parkway. While any improvements in this area should have some positive benefit, the solution to the backups on Cabin John will not come about until 1-495 is widened to eight lanes in Virginia and Maryland and we have ten. lanes on 1-495 between the Parkway interchanges. Virginia's current Six Year Improvement Plan calls for the commencement of the eight lane construction in fiscal year '88-'89. Maryland's draft Consolidated Transportation Program provides for the construction of their eight lanes in fiscal year '89. Hopefully, these projects can be coordinated by the two States whereby a simultaneous completion date for all of the eight laning can be attained. AT LARGE-RURAL 1221 EAST BROAD STREET RICHMOND, 23219 July 27, 1984 J. M. WRAY, JR. CHIEF ENGINEER J. T. WARREN DIRECTOR OF ADMINISTRATION STAT SALLY H. COOPER DIRECTOR OF RAIL AND PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION J. G. RIPLEY DIRECTOR OF PLANNING AND PROGRAMMING Route 123 Adjacent To CIA Headquarters Fairfax County Mr. Shiva K. Pant Director, Office of Transportation County of Fairfax 4100 Chain Bridge Road Fairfax, Virginia 22030 Dear Mr. Pant: Thank you for your letter of July 18 regarding the CIA's off-site road improvements in connection with their expansion program. The engineering studies for these road improvements prepared over the past several months have resulted in two alternatives for improving Route 123. Alternative 2 provides for two at-grade signalized intersections and Alternative 4 provides for grade separation structures at Georgetown Pike and the CIA entrance. Due to the projected traffic volumes for the year 2005, both of these alternatives require six lanes on Route 123. In an effort to reduce citizen opposition to six lanes on Route 123, which has been voiced at the CIA Traffic Advisory Committee meetings, four lanes will be constructed on Route 123 ini- tially and the CIA will implement a traffic management system whereby the existing peak hour vehicle arrival/departure rate at each entrance will not be exceeded. These improvements, plus the CIA's traffic management system, should provide adequate traffic service on Route 123 until the six lanes noted in the Statewide Transportation Plan for the Year 2005 are implemented. However, if the CIA does not enforce their traffic management system, then the agreement provides for CIA funds to be used for adding the third lane on Route 123 from the vicinity of Potomac School Road to Merchants Lane. The present thinking at the Department and CIA is to grade the 123 roadway for the future six lanes when the four lanes are constructed initially.
